summary: Codenames has spymasters giving one-word clues to get their teammates to point at their team's agent words on a 5x5 grid, while avoiding the opponent's agents, bystanders, and especially the assassin. It's a fast, clever party game almost entirely about clever wordplay and reading your teammates' minds.
praised: Extremely easy to teach and endlessly replayable
Great mix of word-association cleverness and tension
Scales well from small groups to large parties
criticised: Relies heavily on shared cultural/language references between teammates
Can be swingy if a team hits the assassin early
Less fun with players who overthink or underthink clues
Imbalanced if one team has a much better clue-giver

interaction.detail: The entire 25-card grid is shared, and one player's clue directly shapes their whole team's guesses each turn, with opposing teams racing against each other on the same board. There's no private player state at all — it's fully public information filtered through hidden knowledge held only by spymasters.

scoring.how_you_win: There are no points; a team wins the instant it has correctly identified all of its own agent cards on the board first, or immediately loses if it touches the assassin.
